recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-12216 unless FHIR-I separately decides to revisit whether DELETE should continue allowing 200 OK responses with payloads.
issue_request: FHIR-12216 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for the FHIR-core HTTP page. It reported that delete guidance first allowed only 204 No Content for successful deletion or a resource that does not exist, while later text allowed 204 or 200 for an already-deleted resource. The resolution required both statements to say 200 OK is used when the response contains a payload and 204 No Content is used when there is no payload.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit 3d7763fc7d0a1a1921562cf73de46c53197d669e, matching the Jira comment that cited svn @10126. That commit changed both DELETE sentences in source/http.html to the current conditional 200 OK with payload / 204 No Content without payload wording.
additional_context: source/http.html is in current build scope through publish.ini, where http.html is listed in [pages]. The latest combined branch still contains the aligned wording at source/http.html:1071-1086. A 2020 Zulip discussion about DELETE and ETag asked what a 200 OK DELETE payload should contain, but did not reverse the Jira decision. Direct FHIR-12216 Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The combined branch already satisfies the published FHIR-12216 resolution, so an empty no-change audit commit was published.
